title: Getting started with bayesqm
text: Q study asks participant rank-order set statements forced distribution. bayesqm represents J × N numeric matrix (statements rows, participants columns) plus vector forced-distribution counts. real study, read_qsort() auto-detects file format: qmethod users can use dotted aliases instead: import.pqmethod(), import.htmlq(), import.kenq(), import.easyhtmlq(). vignette simulate dataset generate_data() wrap qsort_data():

title: Getting started with bayesqm
text: run_bayes() fits model K range applies peak-plus-Sivula protocol: ELPD peak automated choice; Sivula (2025) parsimony rule reported alongside. real data call: vignette use synthetic run produced demo_run(): ELPD across K. Solid = peak (automated choice). Dashed = Sivula. run$case field labels relationship. methods pick K, case agree data supports K unambiguously. ELPD peak exceeds Sivula choice, case gap: richer model fits bit better LOO decisively, choice turn substantive evidence. Sivula picks larger K peak (reversed), something usually gone wrong ELPD comparison ; case rare practice read substantive finding.
code: run <- run_bayes(qdata, K_max = 4, seed = 1,                  chains = 2, iter = 1500, warmup = 800) run <- demo_run(K_max = 4, k_peak = 3, k_sivula = 2, case = "gap") run #> Bayesian Q-methodology: multi-K comparison #>   K range:      1..4 #>   ELPD peak:    K = 3  (automated adoption) #>   Sivula rule:  K = 2  (parsimony diagnostic) #>   Case:         gap  (ELPD peak > Sivula (weak discrimination between adjacent models)) #>  #> LOO comparison: #>  K    elpd   se delta_elpd se_delta ratio #>  1 -180.09 8.00                           #>  2 -170.91 7.00      -9.18     3.00  3.06 #>  3 -165.42 6.00      -5.49     3.00  1.83 #>  4 -170.20 5.00       4.78     3.00  1.59 #>  #> Case 'gap': adopt k_peak if corroborated by external evidence, else fall back to k_sivula for parsimony. plot_elpd(run)

title: Bayesian Q-Methodology Factor Analysis
text: basic workflow three calls: read_qsort() handles common Q-software file formats: CSV Excel (including HTMLQ, FlashQ, tablet exports), PQMethod .DAT, Ken-Q JSON multi-sheet Excel, KADE ZIP, Easy-HTMLQ Firebase JSON. fit_bayesian() returns object class bayesqm_fit behaves like modelling object R: print, summary, coef, fitted, residuals, sigma, .matrix, plot work expect. choose number factors, fit across range K: bayesqm_run object reports peak K (ELPD-optimal choice) Sivula K (parsimony choice). agree, data supports K unambiguously. disagree, gap informative, run_bayes() labels case agree, gap, reversed summary. richer visual views single fit : base-R plots; package hard dependency ggplot2. ggplot2 ggdist installed, autoplot() method registered renders views using stat_pointinterval stat_halfeye. figure export, save_bayesqm_plot() opens right device file extension, caption_bayesqm() returns ready--paste figure caption reports K, N, J, chains, coverage probability, convergence diagnostics.
code: library(bayesqm) qdata <- read_qsort("mystudy.csv") fit   <- fit_bayesian(qdata, K = 3) run <- run_bayes(qdata, K_max = 5) plot_elpd(run) plot_loading_posterior(fit)   # loadings with 50 and 95 percent intervals plot_membership(fit)          # dominant-factor probability heatmap plot_dist_cons(fit)           # distinguishing-statement probability plot_ppc(fit)                 # posterior predictive check plot_tucker(fit)              # MatchAlign alignment quality plot_hyper(fit)               # hyperparameter posteriors

title: Bayesian Q-Methodology Factor Analysis
text: output object deliberately parallels qmethod’s. slot names ($loa, $zsc, $zsc_n, $qdc, $f_char, $flagged) identical, $qdc$dist..cons vocabulary (“Distinguishes ”, “Consensus”, “Distinguishes f1, f3”). Dotted import aliases (import.pqmethod(), import.htmlq(), import.kenq(), import.easyhtmlq()) forward -named readers. Scripts written qmethod can usually ported changing one two function calls. methodology different . qmethod centroid PCA extraction, varimax rotation, Brown’s significance threshold flagging, z-score test distinguishing statements, scree parallel analysis choosing K. bayesqm replaces Bayesian analogue: factor model sampled Stan, MatchAlign rotational alignment, posterior dominance probability flagging, P(|f_jk - f_jl| > δ) distinguishing, peak-plus-Sivula ELPD K selection. output shapes can kept compatible, .

title: Probabilistic factor-membership summaries — bayesqm-membership
text: paper's Section 6 summaries, computed entirely posterior draws: compute_threshold_prob() returns N x K posterior probability |lambda_ik| > threshold, .e. Bayesian version Brown (1980) flagging rule. compute_dominant_prob() returns N x K posterior probability factor k dominant factor participant . compute_distinguishing_prob() returns P(|f_jk - f_jl| > delta) every pair factors. compute_consensus_prob() returns joint probability every factor pair's separation stays delta. classify_membership() turns dominant probabilities per-participant tier verdict (Strong / Moderate / Weak).

title: Probabilistic factor-membership summaries — bayesqm-membership
code: compute_threshold_prob(Lambda_draws, threshold)  compute_dominant_prob(Lambda_draws)  compute_distinguishing_prob(F_draws, delta = 1)  compute_consensus_prob(F_draws, delta = 1)  classify_membership(Lambda_draws, strong = 0.8, moderate = 0.6)

title: Probabilistic factor-membership summaries — bayesqm-membership
text: Lambda_draws Array shape [T, N, K] aligned loading draws. threshold Numeric threshold; natural default 1.96 / sqrt(J) Brown rule. F_draws Array shape [T, J, K] aligned factor-score draws. delta Minimum separation standardized factor-score scale (default 1.0). strong, moderate Tier cutoffs max P(dominant) (defaults 0.80 0.60 following paper).

title: Probabilistic factor-membership summaries — bayesqm-membership
text: compute_threshold_prob(), compute_dominant_prob() return N x K matrices. compute_distinguishing_prob() returns J x choose(K, 2) matrix. compute_consensus_prob() returns length-J named vector. classify_membership() returns data frame.

Fit model. fit_bayesian() returns bayesqm_fit object. run_bayes() fits model range K returns bayesqm_run object carrying ELPD comparison table peak-plus-Sivula protocol verdict. Summarise posterior. compute_loadings(), compute_zscores(), compute_factor_array(), compute_dominant_prob(), compute_threshold_prob(), compute_distinguishing_prob(), compute_consensus_prob(), classify_membership(), compute_posterior_scalars(). Use standard R accessors. coef(), fitted(), residuals(), sigma(), family(), nobs(), .matrix(), .array(), .data.frame(), update(), plus rstantools::posterior_interval() rstantools::prior_summary() work directly fit. title: bayesqm: Bayesian Q-Methodology Factor Analysis — bayesqm-package
text: bayesqm_fit object parallels qmethod::qmethod output meaningful, scripts written qmethod largely keep working: Slot names match: $dataset, $loa, $zsc, $zsc_n, $f_char, $qdc, $flagged. $qdc$dist..cons vocabulary matches exactly ("Distinguishes ", "Consensus", "Distinguishes f1, f3", ""). Dotted reader aliases (import.pqmethod(), import.htmlq(), import.kenq(), import.easyhtmlq()) forward read_* readers. Intentional Bayesian divergences: $f_char$characteristics omits classical test-theory columns (av_rel_coef, reliability, se_fscores, sd_dif). Factor-score uncertainty already quantified posterior credible intervals $ci_lower $ci_upper, Spearman-Brown composite reliability right construct. $flagged logical N x K matrix defined P(argmax_k |Lambda[, k]| = k) > 0.5 rather Brown's (1980) significance-based rule. posterior probability makes Bayesian analogue direct. $brief uses K, N, J (nfactors, nqsort, nstat) includes Bayesian-specific fields (family, prob, priors, backend).
